🇲🇽🛢️ <u>HOW SALINAS AND ZEDILLO MORTGAGED PEMEX TO WALL STREET</u>

NAFTA's Chapter VI opened Mexico's electricity to foreign producers. Chapter X forced Pemex and CFE to give national treatment to US corporations. Pemex workforce: 211,000 in 1988 → 130,000 by 1994. Over 40,600 workers liquidated in a single sexenio.

Then in 1995, Zedillo pledged ALL Pemex oil revenue to the Federal Reserve as loan collateral. Goldman Sachs collected $5.7 billion. Fidelity got $8.5 billion. Every barrel Mexico pumped, Wall Street cashed first. That's the neoliberal legacy the 4T is undoing.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>50 BILLION PESOS — MEXICO'S LARGEST-EVER HIGHWAY INVESTMENT</u>

18,000+ km of highways under rehabilitation. 100,000 jobs being generated. 3,042 public bids launched — 1,703 already awarded for 68 billion pesos. 20 repaving trains covering 4,000 km of federal roads, 11 more coming.

South-Southeast gets the largest share: 10.8 billion pesos, 3,140 km. 888 km of artisanal roads being built in rural and Indigenous communities. Infrastructure money going to the people, not to offshore accounts.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US HOUSE VOTES 215-208 TO END IRAN WAR — TRUMP'S OWN PARTY CRACKS</u>

The House passed a War Powers Resolution directing Trump to withdraw forces from Iran — the first successful such vote since the war began February 28. Four Republicans broke ranks: Massie, Fitzpatrick, Barrett, Davidson.

Three months in. $29 billion spent. The War Powers Act deadline expired May 1 with no congressional authorization. The empire's own legislature is putting Trump's unauthorized war on the record.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"WE'RE IMPRESSED" — US SECURITY CHIEF ACKNOWLEDGES MEXICO'S SOVEREIGNTY</u>

DHS Secretary Mullin told Congress he was "very impressed" with Sheinbaum: "Much more cooperative than the previous administration — but they still believe in their sovereignty, and we must respect that."

Homicides down 49%. 2,400 drug labs dismantled. 71 tons of cocaine seized at sea. Mexico gets results without foreign agents on its soil — and now even Washington has to say it out loud.

🇲🇽🔥🐉 USMCA Round 2: Washington wants Mexico to ban China for them

Mexico and the US restart USMCA talks June 16-17 in Washington. On the table: rules of origin, agriculture, and what the US politely calls "a level playing field." Translation: Washington wants the review to force Mexico — and Canada — into America's containment posture against China.

Mexico already moved: tariffs up to 50% on 1,400 product categories since January, hitting Chinese imports across autos, steel, and electronics. That was leverage for the negotiating table, not capitulation. At Round 1 in Mexico City, Ebrard declared US 50% steel tariffs "unsustainable" — Mexican steel exports to the US are down 36.6%.

The US wants Mexico to pay the cost of America's China problem. Mexico is demanding symmetry: if we close doors to Beijing, you reopen doors to us. Sovereignty as accounting — every concession booked, every demand measured.

🇲🇽🐉🌐 Mexico's port empire: Chinese capital is rebuilding the Pacific gateway

China Harbour Engineering, a Chinese state firm, is rebuilding Veracruz on the Gulf. Manzanillo — Mexico's main Pacific port — is mid-expansion at $2.7 billion, designed to rival the largest ports in the hemisphere. Lázaro Cárdenas just absorbed a $350M upgrade from APM Terminals. Puerto Progreso in Yucatán is next.

The framing matters. Sheinbaum's team doesn't sell this as "Chinese investment." It sells Mexico as "the maritime-terrestrial bridge between Asia, Latin America and North America." T-MEC manufacturing platform yesterday, multipolar logistics hub tomorrow.

While Washington tells Mexico to pick a side, Mexico is quietly upgrading ports for cargo from both. That's what sovereignty looks like in a multipolar world: not loyalty, leverage.

🇲🇽🏭 Mexico is turning invasive Caribbean sargassum into rural roads. The fibers in sargassum absorb tension — making them ideal for stabilizing the base layers of community-built "caminos artesanales." Already in pilot use by the Instituto Mexicano del Transporte. — Jesús Esteva Medina, Secretary of Infrastructure, Mañanera 03/06/2026 In 2026: 6 billion pesos for 388 artisanal roads built in assembly with Indigenous communities across 18 states. Program also uses recovered tire rubber. One invasive species, two solutions: clearing Caribbean coasts + connecting remote villages.

🇲🇽✊ "I was paying 8,000 pesos in rent. Now I pay 4,000 — and the house is mine." Erika Adriana Zaragoza Sánchez, mother of three engineers, received the keys to her new 60-square-meter home at Parques del Triunfo in El Salto, Jalisco — Mexico's electronics manufacturing corridor. — Beneficiary, Programa de Vivienda del Bienestar, 03/06/2026 It was the 25th "Miércoles de Vivienda." 87 developments active nationwide, 21,500 families housed. 13 more open in June. Jalisco's goal raised from 29,500 to 75,743 units; 45.5 billion pesos invested.
